items.title: Possible user confusion from differing zpage information

labels.name: kind/documentation
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to documentation.

labels.name: sig/node
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Node.

labels.name: sig/instrumentation
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Instrumentation.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

items.body:
I've been look at the zpages support which went to beta in 1.36 ( [KEP-4828](https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/blob/master/keps/sig-instrumentation/4828-component-flagz/README.md) ) and I wanted to provide some feedback on where I think the current design might cause some user confusion, based on differences in output between the `/configz` and `/flagz` output.

From reading the KEP and some testing I understand that the `/flagz` endpoint returns the values set by command line flags passed to the component *or* default values where no explicit configuration flag has been passed. In contrast to this `/configz` returns the running configuration of the component taking into account flags, default values, and configuration files.

As a result, where components have values set from configuration files as well as command line flags, the responses from `/flagz` and `/configz` will be different. Looking at a standard Kubeadm 1.36 cluster, in that setup it occurs in the kube-proxy and kubelet components, as the others either don't use configuration files (kube-scheduler and kube-controller) or don't have a `/configz` endpoint (kube-apiserver).

As an example in the kubelet there are several significant differences in what's returned by `/flagz` and `/configz`, some of them are :-

- `/flagz` reports that anonymous authentication is enabled for the kubelet, however this is disabled in the kubelets configuration file, so in reality it is not enabled.
- `/flagz` reports that the cgroupDriver is `cgroupfs` (this is the default, there's no explicit flag set by the component) but the configuration file sets `systemd` which is reported by `/configz`
- `/flagz` reports `rotate-certificates` is `false`, but this is enabled in the configuration file `rotateCertificates` setting.
  
This could be particularly tricky for the `kube-apiserver` as there is no `/configz` endpoints, so no obvious path for cluster admins to check the full running configuration. 

Currently in the [zpages documentation](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/instrumentation/zpages/) there is no mention of `/configz` which may lead to cluster administrators being unaware of its presence or unaware of the difference in output between `/flagz` and `/configz`

As the goal of this feature is to support cluster administrators in diagnosing issues with running clusters, it would be great to explain the differences between these two endpoints, and ensure that they're available for all components.

items.title: client-go: rest_client metrics lack resource dimensions, making client-side observability difficult

labels.name: kind/bug
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a bug.

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: sig/instrumentation
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Instrumentation.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

items.body:
### What happened?

Server-side metrics (e.g. `apiserver_request_duration_seconds`) let you measure latency per verb, resource, group, version, and scope.

However, the client-side metrics exposed by client-go's REST layer use only verb (raw HTTP method) and host as labels. This means:

  - You cannot measure client-side latency per resource. "How long do Pod LIST calls take from the controller's perspective?" is unanswerable.
  - LIST and GET are indistinguishable. The client records the raw HTTP method GET for both. The server distinguishes these as separate verbs.
  - No scope information. You cannot distinguish cluster-scoped from namespace-scoped requests.

Debugging client-side latency is difficult because the metrics lack this information.

We could add resource-aware labels to `rest_client` metrics, similar to what server-side metrics already provide:

1. We could add resource , group, version, and scope labels.
2. We could map HTTP methods to API verbs (GET vs LIST) so verb carries semantic meaning.


Additionally, the recently introduced `A Unified Identity for client-go Components for Enhanced Telemetry` ([xref](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1HUNewBqN3lk2DSHJaxKZmmhYgt0SNgp9AqpJTY6cfRM/edit?resourcekey=0-uIvQ3ezUROHa6OKjWZUzcw&tab=t.0#heading=h.qtaj715knfkg))  for client-go components provides a name label that Informers and Reflectors propagate to identify which component initiated a request. This identity could also be passed into rest_client metrics, allowing to correlate API requests back to the specific component that made them.

items.title: No clean way to apply feature-gate-gated metric options

labels.name: sig/instrumentation
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Instrumentation.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

items.body:
**Problem**

Some metric options (like [native histogram options](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0275382260bc0d5279b703d21ec7ad4db35b8d78/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/internal/nativehistograms.go#L33-L40) supported via `NativeHistograms` feature gate, potentially more in future) need to be applied at metric registration time. Specifically, `initializeMetric()` ([ref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/histogram.go#L96)) reads `NativeHistogramsEnabled()` ([ref](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/opts.go#L210-L214)) when creating the underlying prometheus object, so feature gate state must be known before any metric is registered.
The problem here is that the current registration setup provides no clean way to guarantee this ordering. Metrics packages (workqueue, restclient, leaderelection, fifo) have historically registered themselves via `init()` which fires at import time, well before flags are parsed and feature gates are finalized.
______________________________

**What was tried**

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/137061 attempted to fix this by removing `init()` from those packages and requiring explicit `Register()` calls from each component's `Run()` function, after the feature gates are parsed. This works for in-tree components in `k/k` but introduces 2 problems:

1. Silent breakages for out-of-tree consumers
Projects outside `k/k` (operators, cloud provider controllers, anything using `client-go` or `controller-runtime`) relied on `init()` auto-registration. With it removed, their `workqueue_*`, `rest_client_*` etc. metrics silently disappear with no error or warning

2. `sync.Once` makes correct ordering impossible in practice
The new `Register()` functions use `sync.Once` to prevent double-registration panics, which creates a "first caller wins" problem. Consider an operator built on `controller-runtime`, to avoid breaking its own users, `controller-runtime` must call `Register()` early. That fires the `sync.Once` before feature gates are parsed. Later when the operator calls `Register()` after parsing the feature gates, the call is a silent no-op, consequently native-histograms never get enabled. There is no way for framework authors to avoid this. If they call `Register()` early they block the feature gate from taking effect, if they dont, some other `init()` in the dependency graph may do it instead.
This means the correctness of metric configuration now depends on non-deterministic `init()` ordering across the full transitive dependency graph.
______________________________

**Potential fixes**

1. defer prom metric object creations till after the feature-gates are parsed by making [`legacyregistry`
`legacyregistry.MustRegister`](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/component-base/metrics/legacyregistry/registry.go#L37) enqueue metrics into a pending set rather than immediately calling `initializeMetric()`. When `ApplyFeatureGates()` is called, the registry flushes the pending set, firing `initializeMetric()` for every queued metric, now with the correct feature gate state set. POC: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138453
2. Move creation of metrics from init() funcs to constructors of the objects that use the metrics. This came up after discussion with @liggitt, who suggested a more principled alternative to the above solution -"if we really need to defer constructing metrics to be feature-gate informed, I'd rather just delay that directly instead of trying to allow them to still be constructed early, but held, and then really for real constructed later". POC: https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/138914


Would like to hear any other ideas to fix this issue, since addressing this will establish a clean way to use future feature-gated metric options reliably as well.

items.title: Proposing unification and alignment of apiserver storage metrics (etcd3 and watch cache)

labels.name: sig/api-machinery
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG API Machinery.

labels.name: kind/feature
labels.description: Categorizes issue or PR as related to a new feature.

labels.name: sig/instrumentation
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Instrumentation.

labels.name: triage/accepted
labels.description: Indicates an issue or PR is ready to be actively worked on.

labels.name: sig/etcd
labels.description: Categorizes an issue or PR as relevant to SIG Etcd.

items.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Currently, Kubernetes exposes separate sets of metrics for etcd3 or from the watch cache. Both implement exactly the same interface and methods, but they have totally different metrics. For example, etcd3 exports metric with `apiserver_storage_list_total`,  while the cacher exposes `apiserver_cache_list_total`.

We propose to unify these aligned metrics by introducing a storage label. This would allow users to aggregate metrics across the entire storage layer or filter by specific backend (etcd or watchcache).

**Proposed label**: `storage="etcd|watchcache"`


For example, apiserver_storage_list_total could be unified with a label:

* apiserver_storage_list_total{storage="etcd"}
* apiserver_storage_list_total{storage="watchcache"}

Caveats and Recommendations
* gRPC Metrics vs. Storage Metrics: While etcd client calls are covered by gRPC-level metrics, these are often "unmergable" with application-level concepts like the watch cache. We recommend maintaining aligned metrics at the k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage layer to allow direct comparison of the same logical operations regardless of the serving layer.

## Next Steps

1. Complete the audit of all metrics in [staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/metrics/metrics.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/metrics/metrics.go) and [staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/metrics/metrics.go](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/cacher/metrics/metrics.go).
2. Agree on a final set of unified metric names and labels.
3. Define a deprecation path for the existing fragmented metrics.

### Why is this needed?

This fragmentation hinders observability by:
* Preventing a unified view of storage operations (e.g. type and percentage of request served from etcd).
* Violating [Prometheus best practices](https://prometheus.io/docs/practices/naming/#labels), which recommend using labels to differentiate characteristics of the thing being measured rather than embedding them in the metric name.

/sig instrumentation
